title: California Civil Code Section 1668 (contracts exempting a party from responsibility for fraud, willful injury or violation of law)
publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel
claims: Section 1668 provides that all contracts which have for their object, directly or indirectly, to exempt any one from responsibility for his own fraud, or willful injury to the person or property of another, or violation of law, whether willful or negligent, are against the policy of the law.
The section sits in Title 4, Unlawful Contracts, of Part 2 of Division 3 of the Civil Code.
updateCadence: Unchanged since enactment in 1872 on the page as read; amended only by legislation.
notes: Read in full on the official host 2026-09-30; the section is one sentence. It states a general rule about exculpatory contracts; it is not confined to construction or to indemnity, and the text itself names no exception. Effective: 1872
